tagline.text: Falls, cold springs and handwoven furniture on the northeast coast

location.label: Location
location.text: Sogod, northeastern Cebu Island (about 60 km north of Cebu City)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,000–3,000 (per person, one night, lodging and transport included)

children.text: Sogod is a quiet municipality on the northeast coast, about 60 km north of Cebu City on the Camotes Sea. With Bagatayam Falls and a cold spring within reach of the town, coastal resorts and a handwoven-furniture village, it makes a good half-day outing.
Sogod lies about
60 km

north of Cebu City, bordered by Borbon to the north, Tuburan and Tabuelan to the west, Catmon to the south and the Camotes Sea to the east. The terrain runs from sea level on the coast up to uplands of about 445 m, and its 18 barangays are a mix of coastal and upland ones. The population is about 40,700 (2024 census).

Sogod's history is relatively short. According to Wikipedia, it was merged with Catmon at the request of the American colonial authorities in 1903 and became a separate municipality again in 1921. The 1903 population was a little over 6,000. In February 1966 a shootout killed the mayor, the police chief and others, and in April 2000 about 30 New People's Army rebels raided the municipal hall. Today it is a peaceful coastal town that people visit on weekends from Cebu City and nearby areas.

For travelers, Sogod is a municipality of the sea, water play and small crafts. There are resorts and restaurants along the coast, and from town you can casually visit waterside spots such as Bagatayam Falls and the Binaliw cold spring. The "Weavers of Hope," residents who make handwoven furniture centered on Barangay Liki, are also known and make meaningful souvenirs.
Sogod receives about 1,640 mm of rain a year, and the average daily high is around

. Roads lead north to Borbon, west to Tuburan and south to Catmon, so it works as a midpoint where you can stay a night on a northern Cebu loop. Sogod has no big headline sights, which is exactly why it is a good place to see unpretentious provincial life. A day can be as simple as watching shoppers at the town market in the morning, playing in the falls and spring at midday, and relaxing by the sea in the evening. Combine it with neighboring municipalities to extend your trip and you can see both the east coast and the western uplands of northern Cebu. Public transport is infrequent, so decide on your transport in advance.
The falls are described as about a
30-minute

walk from town. They are not large, but they are a refreshing place to play in the water, with forest and the sound of water together. The path is slippery just after rain, so wear shoes. Do not go near when the water is up, and follow locals' advice if given. On the way you pass village scenery and fields, so it is a nice walk as well.

Described as a cold spring good for swimming and picnics on the edge of a grassy area. It is nice to soak in the cool water on a hot day. There are also reports of a spring said to have healing powers and a Marian shrine in Barangay Bagatayam, but sources differ on which spring it is, so confirm the location and name locally.

The parish of St. James the Great in the center of town is the spiritual heart of the community. Outside Mass times you can stop by quietly and look around the building and plaza. On the parish feast day the town comes alive with events, so join in if your schedule allows. Ask the parish or the municipal office for the exact feast day.

Sacaan Sea Breeze Resort, El Mar Resort, Northsky Beach Resort and North Coast Beach Resort are among those on the coast. Many are places to enjoy the seaside view and meals more than the sand, so check the beach conditions at each resort. In high season prices rise and rooms fill early, so check beach and room photos when you book.
Described as a public space near town. It is suited to an evening stroll and a casual look at local life, but confirm the exact location and facilities locally.
A restaurant that Wikipedia lists among tourist attractions, good for a meal in a coastal-town atmosphere. Check opening hours and the menu locally.

In Barangay Liki, residents make handwoven furniture, and the group is called the "Weavers of Hope." The furniture is bulky and hard to carry, but small pieces make good souvenirs and also help local incomes.
You can watch the sun rise on the east coast. If you stay at a resort, an early-morning walk lets you meet a quiet sea. On cloudy days the sunrise may not be visible, so leave spare time in your day.

A one-night stay at a coastal resort involves long travel, so plan to rest from the first afternoon. To see the sunrise, go to bed early the night before.

Intercity buses pick up and drop off on the road in front of town (the Cebu North Road). Ask the driver or conductor for the exact stop.
For a group, hiring a van or car is convenient for covering the falls and the beach in one day.
Leaving straight from the airport saves time.
When hiring, confirm the total price, waiting time and whether fuel is included before you set out.
Between the town and the beaches, use a tricycle or habal-habal. Negotiate the fare before you ride.
The dry season from December to May is best. The falls and springs are clear and the coastal road is stable.
In the rainy season the falls carry more water, but paths are slippery and sea conditions are unstable. Do not enter rivers or gorges when it rains.

Lodging centers on coastal resorts, and the level of rooms and beach facilities differs from place to place. On weekends many local families visit, so reservations are needed. There may be small guesthouses in town, so check reviews in a map app.

Grilled fish and shrimp at coastal restaurants and Filipino home cooking in town are the basics. Some restaurants, such as Northern Aire Restaurant, have good views. At the provincial town market you can buy fruit and snacks cheaply.
When going to the falls or springs, bring water and snacks of your own. There may be few shops there.

Sogod does not have much nightlife or shopping aimed at outsiders. The atmosphere winds down early after dark, so it is realistic to have dinner before sunset and spend late nights at your lodging. You can buy medicine and necessities at pharmacies and shops in town, but there is no big supermarket, so bring what you need from Cebu City.
The paths to the falls and springs are slippery just after rain, so wear non-slip shoes.
Bring a swimsuit, towel and spare clothes, and leave valuables at your lodging.
Check the last bus time and plan your return first.
Bring plenty of cash. There are few ATMs and places that take cards.
Handwoven furniture is large, so buy mostly small pieces.
Swimming conditions at resort beaches vary with the tide, so ask your lodging.
We recommend combining Bagatayam Falls and the spring in one morning round and resting at the beach in the afternoon.
The town market is liveliest in the morning. Try some simple local snacks.
At falls and springs the water level can suddenly rise when it rains and the bottom is slippery, so do not enter on bad-weather days.
The mountain roads have many bends and can be dangerous when it rains.
Many beaches have no lifeguards, so be careful with children.
Some road and facility conditions may have changed after the September 2025 Cebu earthquake.
Mobile signal can be weak in the mountains, so prepare offline maps.
Coastal resorts can raise prices sharply in high season, so confirm the total before booking.
In the rainy and typhoon seasons, roads can be cut and buses reduced. Leave slack in your schedule.
